filesFromSkeletonNote: The third list, added for #1150: files whose canonical copy lives in the SKELETON that matches the receiving repo's flavour, keyed to the policy for a repo that already holds one. Added because eleven of seventeen estate repos held NEITHER `AGENTS.md` NOR `CLAUDE.md` -- not a stale copy, nothing -- so an agent opening `tabsii-crm` got no worktree discipline, no honest-push rule, no never-merge-red and no reproduce-before-fixing. `files` creates but cannot remap a path, and the satellite ruleset is emphatically NOT this repo's root `AGENTS.md` (that one carries section 9 distribution, `core-manifest.json` and the upgrade flow, none of which applies to a satellite). `filesIfPresent` remaps but deliberately never creates, which is the one thing a backfill must do. Why this is a third list rather than `files` learning the `target -> source` map form, which was the cheaper-looking option: (1) THE SOURCE IS NOT ONE FILE. `_skeletons/plugin-template/AGENTS.md` legitimately differs from `_skeletons/sibling-template/AGENTS.md` by 50 lines -- the birth-time branch-protection and runner-grant checklist from #714, which exists because both plugin repos once ran with no branch protection at all. A single-source map would either delete that from the plugin repos or force it into every sibling, and `shared-files-parity.test.ts` would fail either way, since it requires every `files` entry byte-identical in EVERY skeleton and these two must not be. So the source is resolved per repo from its marker via `skeletonForMarker`. (2) THE TWO FILES NEED OPPOSITE POLICIES ON AN EXISTING COPY. `AGENTS.md` must be kept in step -- it drifting 68 lines behind in tabsii is #559, the founding injury of this whole mechanism -- so it is `sync`. `CLAUDE.md` must not be: its load-bearing content is the `@AGENTS.md` import, but it also carries a per-repo `What this repo is` paragraph, and four of the repos being backfilled (`biffo-runners`, `tabsii-runners`, `tabsii-map`, `tabsii-data-model-design`) are not sibling apps at all, so a one-way overwrite would assert in each of them that they are `a Biffo sibling app (ADR-0007)` whose identity lives in a `biffo.sibling.json` they do not have. `seed` means create where absent and never touch again; `--check` therefore reports a `seed` entry only when it is MISSING, because a differing copy is the repo exercising the ownership `seed` grants it. Repos with no marker (`biffo-runners`, `tabsii-runners`, `tabsii-map`, `tabsii-data-model-design`, in scope via the `scripts/verify.sh` clause) fall back to `skeletonDefault`. That is correct for `AGENTS.md`: the satellite ruleset is dev-branch, worktrees, Conventional Commits, PRs, never-merge-red, honest pushes and security -- it contains NO deploy clause, so there is nothing in it a repo without a deploy would need trimmed, and a trimmed variant would be a second document differing from the first by zero rules. `idea-corpus` is deliberately absent from all of this: it has no git remote, no `dev`, no CI and no branch protection, so every rule in the document would be unsatisfiable there and an agent's first act would be to flag a non-issue -- it needs a remote and a `dev` branch before it can carry the estate ruleset at all. ADDED 2026-08-09 (#1343): `.prettierrc` and `.prettierignore`, both `seed`. Nothing distributed formatting rules to a satellite, so each one either invents its own or runs prettier's own defaults -- measured directly in tabsii-ui#24, where prettier's defaults reformatted all 7 files it touched and this repo's own settings reformatted 3, i.e. a satellite adopting prettier drifts AWAY from the estate rather than towards it. Measured at `origin/dev` across all 14 in-scope satellites before choosing a mechanism (`excludes`'s `tabsii-lms` aside): only 2 held `.prettierrc` at all -- `tabsii-app` (byte-identical to this repo's own root copy, INCLUDING `"plugins": ["prettier-plugin-tailwindcss"]`) and `tabsii-ui` (the tabsii-ui#24 copy, already plugin-free). Zero held `.prettierignore`. Why not `files`: it would copy THIS repo's own root `.prettierrc` verbatim, and that copy carries the Tailwind plugin key for this repo's own portal -- landing it in the 13 satellites with no `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` devDependency does not merely miss the point, it makes `prettier` error outright (`Cannot find module 'prettier-plugin-tailwindcss'`), turning a harmless gap into a hard failure. That is why the canonical copy has to be a SKELETON file rather than this repo's own: it needs different content from a config that must keep the plugin. Why not `sync`: it would overwrite `tabsii-app`'s copy on every run, deleting the plugin key that repo genuinely needs (it has the dependency installed and uses Tailwind classes) -- a one-way overwrite with no per-repo exclusion is exactly what `AGENTS.md` §9 warns `mustBeUniform` exists to avoid, and `seed` sidesteps the need for that: it creates where absent and never touches an existing copy again, so `tabsii-app`'s legitimate divergence is never reported as drift or clobbered. Why not `filesIfPresent`: its whole job is to keep an EXISTING copy in step, never create one -- with only 2 of 14 satellites holding the file, that would leave the other 12 exactly as unprotected as before, which is the gap this issue is about, not a fix for it; and being a one-way overwrite with no per-repo exclusion, it has the identical `tabsii-app` clobbering problem `sync` does. overridesFloorNote:
A FLOOR on `pnpm.overrides`, not a uniformity rule. For each entry, every applicable repo holding <target> must declare at least the override KEYS that <canonical> declares. Extra keys are fine — a repo may pin something the skeleton has no reason to. A MISSING key is the defect, because an override is a security floor and its absence is indistinguishable from 'we never needed it'.

Why this exists: `pnpm.overrides` lives inside package.json, which is legitimately per-repo (name, scripts, deps), so none of the four file lists can carry it — `files` and `filesIfPresent` are whole-file overwrites and would clobber everything around the key. There was therefore NO channel at all, and the cost was measured rather than theoretical: on 2026-08-07 five tabsii repos sat on a js-yaml advisory the template had fixed the day before, biffo-platform-app hit the same one hours later, and nanoid then reddened the estate on 2026-08-08. Every one was found because CI happened to run, not because anything looked.

This DETECTS; it does not write. Distribution is the larger half (biffo-template#1352) and wants a key-level merge that no existing list can express. Reporting the gap the day it appears is most of the value and none of the risk.

The two are complementary, not competing -- this list catches a key MISSING outright (five tabsii repos silently lacking a js-yaml/nanoid pin the template already held); `keyMustBeUniform` catches the key present in every repo but disagreeing on its VALUE (#1367's four-way `undici` bound split), which a presence-only floor cannot see -- every repo but one already had the key, they simply disagreed about it. See `keyMustBeUniformNote` for the fuller reasoning and why it also folds absence into the same measurement as one more disagreeing value, so a repo this floor already reports MISSING is not a blind spot for that list either.

ADDITIVE DELIVERY BUILT 2026-08-09 (biffo-template#1352, the issue's own remaining scope): `scripts/shared-sync.sh --deliver-overrides` now exists and calls a new `apply_overrides_floor()` shell function to actually write the ABSENCE half this list detects. It is deliberately narrower than 'distribution' in general -- it adds a key `<canonical>` declares that a holder is MISSING outright, via a textual splice immediately after the `"overrides": {` line so no other byte of the file moves, verified by re-parsing the result before it is written; it NEVER touches a key the holder already has, whatever its value. That restriction is what makes it safe against the reasoning `keyMustBeUniformNote` records for why writing stayed unbuilt: the risk of a one-way overwrite destroying evidence about which copy is right is scoped to a key that is PRESENT and disputed (`sharp`'s three-way split was exactly that, before #1380/#1381 reconciled it by hand) -- it does not apply to a key that is simply absent, because there is no existing value to destroy. Proving the push+PR path safe means running it against a real satellite, which the pass that built this was explicitly told not to do; wiring that up is named follow-up work, not a bar this change already clears. keyMustBeUniformNote: ADDED 2026-08-08 (#1352, #1367): the sixth list -- fifth is `overridesFloor` immediately above, added earlier the same morning -- and the only one besides `mustBeUniform` that measures a SUBTREE of a file rather than the whole thing, and the only one that never writes. `mustBeUniform` compares a file's blob SHA, so it can only ever say 'identical' or 'not' about the entire file -- exactly wrong for `apps/frontend/package.json`, whose `name`/`version`/`dependencies` are legitimately per-repo while its `pnpm.overrides` (the estate's mechanism for pinning a transitive dependency above a security advisory) must not be. `keyMustBeUniform` maps `<file> -> <dotted key path> -> baseline variant count`, canonicalises the JSON VALUE at that key path (object keys sorted recursively, so field order cannot manufacture a false variant) in every repo that holds the FILE, and counts distinct canonical values -- same ratchet posture as `mustBeUniform` in every other respect: baselines seeded from a real `origin/<base>` measurement, `--check` fails a path only when its LIVE variant count EXCEEDS the baseline, pre-existing residue never hard-blocks, a count that drops below baseline is reported as improved and told to lower it, and only `origin/<base>` refs are ever read, never a working tree. Key path segments are dot-separated and traversed as plain object-property lookups; today's one entry (`pnpm`, `overrides`) contains no literal dots in either segment, so a naive split is exact. A key path whose segment must itself contain a literal dot would need a different separator or an escaping convention -- deliberately not built until an entry actually needs it (YAGNI), and this note is where the limitation is recorded so the next author does not discover it by a silent mis-split. THE UNIT COMPARED IS THE WHOLE VALUE AT THE KEY PATH, not an enumeration of known override names -- `pnpm.overrides` is a single JSON object, so a brand-new override key ADDED anywhere (skeleton or a sibling) changes that repo's canonical value and is caught as a new variant with no manifest edit required to see it; only the DECISION to track a *different* key path (a key path not yet declared here) needs a new entry, exactly as a new file needs a new `mustBeUniform` entry. Not a replacement for `overridesFloor`: that list is built specifically for the ABSENCE half of the class (missing key = defect, checked in one direction, distributable in spirit even though it does not write yet) and already caught tabsii-intake's missing `undici@<7.29.0` on its first run; this list is built for the DIVERGENCE half -- present everywhere, disagreeing on value -- which a presence-only floor structurally cannot see, and it folds absence into the same measurement as one more disagreeing value rather than treating it as a separate signal, so the two reports corroborate on tabsii-intake rather than duplicate blindly. MEASURE-ONLY, LIKE `mustBeUniform`, NOT YET DISTRIBUTED -- decided deliberately, not by default. `mustBeUniform`'s reason (a one-way overwrite of a diverged file destroys evidence about which copy is right) applies at smaller blast radius to a KEY rather than a whole file, but it still applies: measuring `pnpm.overrides` as a whole subtree surfaced a divergence nobody had asked about -- `sharp@<0.35.0`'s value is `^0.35.0` in three siblings and `>=0.35.0` in three others, discovered only because this measurement reads the whole object rather than one known key, and nothing here establishes which bound is deliberate and which is stale. It goes live the day 0.36.0 ships, because `^0.35.0` on a 0.x package means `>=0.35.0 <0.36.0` -- npm's caret locks the MINOR below 1.0.0, which is not what a reader assuming ordinary caret behaviour expects, and is the same 0.x caret trap that made `^0.2.2` unable to reach 0.3.0 elsewhere in this estate the same week. SECOND ENTRY ADDED 2026-08-08: `apps/frontend/package.json` -> `engines`, seeded at 1 from a real `origin/dev` measurement AFTER the six sibling PRs landed, not predicted before them -- `--check` reports `uniform across 6 repos`. acceptedReductionsNote:
ADDED 2026-08-13 (#1577). The escape hatch for the shared-file reduction guard, and the ONLY way to make it pass over a real content loss. Shape: `<target path in the satellite>` -> `<test title>` -> `<why the loss is intended>`. Empty is the correct steady state: an entry here says a sync is knowingly about to DELETE a named test from every satellite that holds that path.

Why the hatch has to exist at all: the guard treats a test RENAMED upstream as one title lost and one gained, because a rename and a deletion are the same event to a reader of the satellite. Without a declaration, an honest rename would be unshippable -- and a guard people cannot ship past is one they route around, which is the argument scripts/check-closing-keywords.mjs already makes about its own path list. Declaring the loss keeps it a decision somebody wrote down rather than a diff nobody read.

Why it is a MAP to a reason and not a list of paths: `filesIfPresent` was silent for exactly this reason -- a whole-file mapping said nothing about content. A path-level opt-out would restore that silence one level up, disarming the guard for every future edit to the file rather than for the one loss being accepted. A declared title stops applying the moment the title changes again.

The guard still COUNTS and PRINTS accepted losses; they leave the failure, not the report. See cli/src/lib/shared-file-reduction-guard.ts for what the guard does and, stated explicitly there, the substantial list of what it does not catch -- it compares test titles in TS/JS test files only, so an accepted-reductions entry is meaningless for any other kind of file.
excludesNote: Repos removed from the measured set, with the reason stated. Read this as a DENOMINATOR CHANGE, not a tidy-up: every mode that walks the estate stops seeing these repos, so a number that improves the day one is added has not improved -- the set it was measured over got smaller. That is the exact failure scripts/protection-audit.sh was rewritten to remove (#1145), where four repos answering 404 were dropped and '27 branches checked, all protected' was a true statement about a set that silently excluded the repos least likely to be protected. So exclusion is DECLARED here rather than inferred at runtime, carries a reason, and is PRINTED on every run -- a check may shrink its scope, but it may never do so quietly. Only add a repo that genuinely cannot receive a change; 'we have not got to it yet' is drift and belongs in the count.

excludes.tabsii-lms: archived 2026-08-06 (github.com/tabsii-com/tabsii-lms) -- read-only, so it can never take a distributed file or converge on a mustBeUniform path. Its copies are frozen at whatever they were on the day it was archived. Retiring under ADR-0108; LMS is now a section of tabsii-crm.

requiresCiStepNote: The other direction of the same audit: a path a repo HOLDS, and the CI step that must therefore run over it. `supersedes` catches a repo running the wrong command; this catches a repo running no command at all. Added for #1244, where _skeletons/plugin-template/ shipped a whole terraform/ module and a ci.yml with no terraform step, so every plugin repo was scaffolded with Terraform nothing checked -- confirmed live in biffo-plugin-idea-scout (3 .tf files, zero terraform references across three workflows). The skeleton fix only ever helps repos created afterwards, and ci.yml cannot be a one-way overwrite (see supersedesNote), so the mechanism has to be an assertion here too. scripts/verify.sh cannot substitute: its terraform check is guarded by `ci_has "terraform fmt"` so a template-shipped gate never asserts over more than the repo's own CI does (the #325 trap), which means a repo whose CI checks nothing correctly gets nothing locally either -- the local half and the CI half only close the hole together. Key is a shell glob relative to the repo root; value is a fixed string that must appear on a non-comment, non-`name:` line of some workflow, so neither an explanatory comment nor a step called "Terraform fmt check" can satisfy it. Add a pair here whenever holding a class of file implies a gate; the check only fires in repos that actually hold a matching path, so a repo with no terraform/ is never reported.
supersedesNote: Raw commands each shared script replaces, checked by scripts/ci-wiring-audit.sh. shared-sync.sh gets the script INTO a repo; nothing made the repo call it, and on 2026-07-29 eleven repos merged the scripts and every one carried on running the raw command -- drift went to zero and the outcome did not move (#884). ci.yml cannot be a one-way overwrite because the path depends on that step's working-directory, so the mechanism is an assertion rather than a copy: you cannot write the line for the repo, but you can refuse to let it forget. Add a pair here whenever a shared script supersedes a command repos invoke directly; the check only fires in repos that actually hold the script, so a repo shared-sync has not reached yet is reported once, by shared-sync, rather than twice.
skeletonAdoptionNote: The fifth list, added for #1271: `<skeleton>:<path>` -> the number of applicable repos that currently hold it. `shared-sync.sh --skeleton-adoption` enumerates every path each repo skeleton owns and reports any not held by ALL of its applicable repos, then ratchets against these numbers. It exists because the estate's other detector, `--candidates`, reports a path only once >=5 repos hold it -- so the LESS adopted something was, the LESS visible it became, and the signal ran backwards against need. This list does not sample; the skeleton's own file list is known, so it enumerates. POSTURE, copied deliberately from `mustBeUniform` above and the core-upgrade orphan ratchet: pre-existing residue NEVER hard-blocks, only a REGRESSION does. A count below its baseline fails the run; a count above it is reported as improved and told to lower the baseline, because a ratchet that never tightens stops meaning anything. A NEW unadopted skeleton path with no baseline also fails -- otherwise a skeleton could gain a file nobody adopts and nothing would notice, which is the #1271 blind spot reappearing one level up. Keyed by `<skeleton>:<path>` rather than path alone because the same path legitimately differs between skeletons: `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` is 7/7 in sibling-template and 0/2 in plugin-template, and a path-only key would conflate two different facts. Measured from each repo's `origin/<base>` via `git ls-tree`, NEVER a working tree -- a stray `.venv/` in the skeleton once turned this report from 26 rows into 10,994 (#1298). NOT listed here, and deliberately: paths matching a skeleton's `.scaffold-tokens.json` are template payload that `biffo plugin create` renames (`src/example_plugin/main.py` -> `src/idea_scout/main.py`), so 0 adoption is CORRECT for them and they are reported in their own section. Deleting them would break plugin scaffolding outright. By contrast `apps/frontend/src/lib/auth-gate.tsx` (3/7) IS deliberate -- it is where apps are meant to differ, per the mustBeUniformNote above -- and its baseline records that rather than inviting a backfill.
